t-7500.author: helix_dev
t-7500.title: The case for keyboard-driven workflows: why your mouse is slowing you down
t-7500.body: Years of optimizing for the keyboard have made me about 30% faster at common tasks. I keep an Emacs config and a terminal multiplexer open at all times. But I also notice that this optimization makes switching between tools slower, not faster. The cost of context switching dwarfs the gains from one tool being optimized.

replies.author: kbrandt
replies.body: Context switching is the real problem. Once you commit to a stack, the gains are real. But the first two weeks are painful.

replies.author: throwaway_sim
replies.body: Two weeks is optimistic. I spent a month on my vim config and it was still slower than just using IDE shortcuts.

replies.author: helix_dev
replies.body: The config was not the problem, your muscle memory was. Give it another month.

t-7501.author: dbstats
t-7501.title: Selecting a time-series database in 2026: the ecosystem has matured
t-7501.body: Five years ago you had three choices. Today there are dozens, each with their own tradeoffs. I evaluated the top ten for a project storing 2 billion points per day. The write performance is not the constraint anymore. The constraint is operational overhead: backups, upgrades, query debugging.

replies.author: rscrypt
replies.body: Operational overhead is the underrated problem. Most evaluations just benchmark write throughput and call it a day.

replies.author: kbrandt
replies.body: Agreed. Running anything at scale is 90% operational. The performance was solved five years ago.

t-7502.author: swixchk
t-7502.title: I tried to replace React and I regret it
t-7502.body: Spent six weeks migrating a dashboard from React to a lightweight alternative. The new framework was smaller and faster, but the ecosystem cost more than the code savings. Debugging tools, tutorials, team knowledge, third-party libraries. We moved it back after two months.

replies.author: tomw
replies.body: The ecosystem is the moat. React is not better, it is just older and bigger.

replies.author: jrnebrach
replies.body: I would argue that the ecosystem tools are actually good. Vite, React Query, Zustand. These came from real problems and are better than homegrown.

t-7503.author: rscrypt
t-7503.title: A vulnerability in X.509 certificate validation that affected everything for six months
t-7503.body: Most of the cryptography libraries we use got the details of certificate validation subtly wrong. The chain of reasoning was sound but the edge case was not tested. This is why we run security audits, and this is why audits are expensive.

replies.author: kbrandt
replies.body: The fact that this was not caught earlier is the real story. Certificate validation has been a solved problem for decades.

replies.author: throwaway_sim
replies.body: Solved in theory. In practice, each implementation gets it wrong. The RFCs are dense and the edge cases are not obvious until they bite you in production.

t-7504.author: dbstats
t-7504.title: Ask HN: What non-tech skill made the biggest impact on your career?
t-7504.body: I realized recently that my career growth accelerated when I learned to write clearly and present well. The technical skill was always there but nobody knew about it. What non-coding skill made the most difference for you?

replies.author: helix_dev
replies.body: Reading the problem statement correctly the first time. I skip too much and have to reread. Learning to slow down and read carefully saved me hours every week.

replies.author: swixchk
replies.body: Learning to say no. Saying yes to everything kills your ability to do anything well.

replies.author: jrnebrach
replies.body: This. Protecting your time and focus is more valuable than any skill you can learn.
